note.note:
Action Plan:
1. Acute lower abdominal pain / suspected urinary tract infection: Prescription for a 3-day course of oral antibiotics sent to the patient’s nominated pharmacy; patient advised to start treatment immediately upon collection. (Antibiotic name and dose/route/frequency not documented—ensure non-penicillin choice because of amoxicillin allergy.)
2. Safety-netting: Patient instructed to seek urgent review if pain worsens, develops fever >38 °C, back/flank pain, new or worsening urinary symptoms, or any other new concerns. Telephone or in-person appointment to be arranged as needed.
3. Follow-up: If symptoms persist or recur after completion of antibiotics, arrange face-to-face assessment including physical examination and urinalysis ± culture.
4. Lifestyle advice: Encourage adequate oral hydration while unwell; limit alcohol until recovery.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: 2-day history of mid-lower abdominal (“lower tummy”) pain.  
• Associated symptoms: Feels hot/sweaty; mild nausea (no vomiting); pink-tinged urine noticed once; urinary frequency ↑; thirst ↑; constipation last week (resolved). Denies dysuria, back/flank pain, diarrhoea, upper-abdominal pain, reflux, vaginal discharge, inter-menstrual or post-coital bleeding.  
• Past medical history: None significant.  
• Surgical/gynecological history: Contraceptive implant in situ for one year, now removed (one year ago). Regular menses.  
• Medications: None regular. No over-the-counter products.  
• Allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction type not specified).  
• Family history: Mother—breast cancer (early, successfully treated).  
• Social: Lives with parents. Non-smoker. Alcohol: ~1 beer on 4 days/week. No recent travel.

Objective:
• Self-recorded temperature: 37 °C one hour prior to consult.  
• No other vital signs or physical examination performed (remote consult).  
• No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Issue: Lower abdominal pain with hematuria / suspected urinary tract infection  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (High likelihood per DDx).  
   - Differential diagnosis:  
     • Urolithiasis (Medium likelihood)—hematuria & pain but lack of colicky flank pain argues against.  
     • Early appendicitis (Low-Medium)—pain location fits early stage; hematuria makes less likely.  
     • Pelvic inflammatory disease (Low)—no vaginal symptoms.  
   - Investigations: None ordered today; consider urine dipstick & culture, pregnancy test, renal USS if symptoms persist (not discussed today).  
   - Treatment: 3-day course of oral antibiotics (name/dose/route/frequency not documented; must avoid penicillins).  
   - Relevant referrals: None today; consider urology or general surgery referral if alternative diagnosis suspected on reassessment.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: Blood pressure, heart rate, abdominal and pelvic examination, urine dip/culture, pregnancy test given reproductive age, documentation of antibiotic choice/dose, documentation of reaction details for amoxicillin allergy.  
• Transcript/plan conflict: Antibiotic class not specified—must avoid amoxicillin due to documented allergy (conflict noted if penicillin intended).  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional minor audio gaps but clinical content understood.
